newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Relatives of top Khmer Rouge defect in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Relatives of top Khmer Rouge defect in Cambodia.

text.p: Three relatives of top Khmer Rouge hardliners defected to the Cambodian government on Wednesday and will arrive in Phnom Penh later in the day, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said.

Ta Mut, son of northern rebel commander Ta Mok, and Ny Korn and Son Chhum, brothers of top hardliner Son Sen, joined the government in a ceremony at midday in this northwest town five km (three miles) from the Thai border.
A helicopter carrying the three men was expected in Phnom Penh later in the day.
The Khmer Rouge, who led the brutal 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime, have been weakened by massive defections in the past several months.
Only about 800 to 2,000 hardliners, including Son Sen, are believed to remain at the hardline base of Anlong Veng.
Hun Sen said in Sampou Luon he had invited the three men to visit the capital after welcoming them to the government.
The three are from Front 250, which defected to the government in early November.
Ta Mut, Ny Korn and Son Chhum did not defect at the time, leaving themselves isolated, analysts said.

Ta Mut and Ny Korn were thought to have been seized by breakaway commander Ei Chien in his northwest base at Pailin. They later were reported to have escaped to Thailand, only to be returned to Ei Chien in Pailin.
But former Khmer Rouge Commander Him Put of Front 250 said Ta Mut and Son Chhum had been most recently in southeast Cambodia, where they had escaped to Koh Kong.
Ny Korn had apparently remained in Pailin until a few days ago.
"I escaped from Pailin three days ago and arrived here," he told Reuters. "I am no longer a commander...but I don't need a position any more. My fate will depend on the government."
Son Chhum said he hoped the defections of the three men would encourage Son Sen, who is at Anlong Veng, to join the government.
"I would like to appeal to my brother Son Sen to join with the government and stop fighting," he told Reuters.
Son Sen commanded the final Khmer Rouge assault in 1975 when the guerrillas took Phnom Penh.
The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N.-sponsored peace pact in 1991, but later reneged on the deal and have been fighting the coalition government which took office after elections in 1993.
